title: SRD coverage: dinosaurs and prehistoric beasts
summary: Independently authored GURPS builds for the 6 prehistoric identities issue #41 enumerates. Size Modifier comes from the published table keyed to longest dimension, which for these animals is nose-to-tail and puts three of them past the point where the Strength discount for size bottoms out. ST comes from Basic Lift and from what the animal demonstrably shifts — a carcass carried, a rival shoved, a body torn free — rather than from raw tonnage, which would produce numbers no table could use. The two marine reptiles declare water as their primary medium; the four land animals do not, and their sprint is stated in the notes rather than folded into the published Move.

monsters.name: Deinonychus
monsters.lair: A scrape in dense scrub, shared by the pack and stinking of old kills.

attacks.name: Sickle Claw
attacks.notes: The inner toe claw, brought down while the animal holds on with its hands and jaws. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: Man-high, feathered and far too interested in the party. Deinonychus hunt in company, and they are among the very few animals that will work out where a group is going and be waiting there. They come in from more than one side. The one making noise is not the one to watch.
notes: The pack is the threat. Run these as a coordinated group.
provenanceNotes: About ten feet nose to tail, which is the SM +1 row; most of that is tail.
ST from Basic Lift: it holds down and tears apart something its own size.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Elasmosaurus
monsters.lair: None; open water, and whatever shoal it is following.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Delivered at the end of a neck longer than the rest of the animal. It can take someone off a deck without the body ever entering the water.

monsters.description: Forty-five feet of marine reptile, twenty-five of it neck. It swims under a boat and surfaces alongside, and the head arrives from a direction nobody was watching. The body is barely a threat on its own; the reach is the whole animal, and there is no safe distance from it short of dry land.
provenanceNotes: Forty-five feet, which is the SM +5 row — the top of the published table's practical range for a creature at a table.
Reach is the point of the build. The bite is stated at reach C,4 because the neck, not the jaws, is what makes this dangerous.

monsters.name: Megaraptor
monsters.lair: A trampled clearing at the center of a range it has cleared of everything else.

attacks.name: Sickle Claw
attacks.notes: A claw the length of a shortsword on each foot. Cannot parry.

monsters.description: The deinonychus problem at five times the weight: sixteen feet of hunting animal that still moves in company and still thinks about angles. A tyrannosaur can be survived by being somewhere else. A pair of megaraptors has to be fought.
provenanceNotes: Sixteen feet nose to tail, which is the SM +2 row.
ST from Basic Lift: it tears a limb off something the weight of a horse.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Plesiosaurus
monsters.lair: A deep coastal bay it works from end to end.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: A mouth full of interlocking needles, delivered on a neck that reaches over a gunwale.

monsters.description: Fifteen feet of barrel-bodied reptile rowing itself along on four flippers, with a neck that arrives before the rest of it does. It hunts fish and holds no particular opinion about people, right up until a boat sits between it and the shoal.
provenanceNotes: Fifteen feet, which is the SM +2 row.
ST from Basic Lift: it carries off a 265 lb. piece of whatever it took.

monsters.name: Triceratops
monsters.lair: None; the herd walks a circuit between water and browse.

attacks.name: Horns
attacks.notes: Two brow horns three feet long, driven by ten tons at a run.

monsters.description: Ten tons of armored herbivore with a bone shield over the neck and two horns that have been used on worse. It does not hunt, and it does not need clever provocation — walking between a cow and a calf will do. The charge covers ground faster than ten tons has any business covering it.
notes: The frill is bone, but it covers the neck alone and the published DR is a whole-body figure. A GM who wants the frill to count should treat it as cover for the neck rather than raise DR.
provenanceNotes: Thirty feet nose to tail, which is the SM +4 row.
ST from Basic Lift: it shoves aside a rival of its own species, which is the heaviest thing it ever does on purpose.
Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Peripheral Vision. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Tyrannosaurus
monsters.lair: None. Its range is whatever it is currently standing in.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Takes a whole person, or a whole horse, and does not need a second attempt. Jaws that crack bone as a matter of routine.

monsters.description: Forty feet of animal whose only real predator is another one of itself. It smells a party long before it sees them, and it neither stalks nor tests: it walks straight in, because nothing in its experience has ever been worth caution. Parties survive it with distance and broken ground rather than with tactics.
provenanceNotes: Forty feet nose to tail, which is the SM +5 row.
ST from Basic Lift: it lifts and shakes a carcass the weight of a horse, which is the heaviest thing it demonstrably does. Tonnage would give a larger figure that no encounter could use.
At this Size Modifier the published Strength discount for size has bottomed out, so the racial template prices ST at the floor of its cost rather than lower.

The bite is impaling rather than cutting. A tyrannosaur's teeth are thick conical pegs built to punch through bone and hold, not serrated blades — which is what separates it from the dromaeosaurs, whose teeth genuinely are knives.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Night Vision; the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.
